benchmark.command: (cd client-wasm && wasm-pack build --target nodejs --release) && node client-wasm/benchmark.mjs 30 paper/experiments/reconstruction_wasm.csv
benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95 after one untimed warm-up proof
benchmark.clock: js_sys::Date::now wall-clock milliseconds inside the wasm32 boundary

native_benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95

component_profile.aggregation: median over 30 samples; nanoseconds in component CSV
component_profile.sum_tolerance: component sums may exceed total by at most 25 percent because stages are timed in separate calls

scoped_baseline.scope: single-slot arithmetic selector relation only; excludes ElGamal, shuffle, cross-key proofs, authenticated state, and dropout composition
scoped_baseline.toolchain: Circom 2.2.3, snarkjs 0.7.5, BN128, local throwaway Powers of Tau

multislot_baseline.scope: finite-domain multi-slot exact-coverage and slot-membership arithmetic; excludes curve ElGamal, cross-key group equations, Bayer-Groth, authenticated state, and protocol composition
multislot_baseline.toolchain: Circom 2.2.3, snarkjs 0.7.5, BN128, local throwaway Powers of Tau

curve_level_baseline.shape: n=52, k=13, 30 samples after one untimed warm-up
curve_level_baseline.scope: same curve-generic reconstruction relation with BN254 ElGamal, cross-key proofs, Bayer-Groth, slot OR proofs, exact coverage, and a measured BN254 Borsh v3 codec; not the production StarkCurve Poseidon/browser wire path

statement_schema_refinement.scope: full deterministic statement and seeded proof-instance wire schemas; proof bytes remain randomized across fresh runs

network_benchmark.collection: Chrome DevTools Protocol with browser cache cleared and disabled before every run
network_benchmark.scope: historical cache-disabled code download, resource timing, module initialization, and one n=52,k=13 proof per run before binary upload support; superseded by the upload benchmark for current wire behavior

network_upload_benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95 over 30 independent cache-disabled page loads with binary proof uploads
network_upload_benchmark.collection: Chrome DevTools Protocol with browser cache cleared and disabled before every run; server decodes and cryptographically verifies each uploaded bundle
network_upload_benchmark.scope: historical cache-disabled code download plus cryptographically verified binary proof upload over loopback, recorded before service-worker support changed the upload page; superseded for transport comparison by the same-source HTTP/TLS pair

network_service_worker_benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95 over 30 warm service-worker page loads with binary proof uploads
network_service_worker_benchmark.collection: Chrome DevTools Protocol; one service-worker bootstrap load before measurement, then 30 controlled pages controlled by the warmed service worker; proof upload and result submission bypass the cache
network_service_worker_benchmark.scope: warm service-worker cache hits for HTML/JavaScript/WASM plus cryptographically verified proof upload over loopback; not cold service-worker install, browser HTTP-cache behavior, cold TCP, TLS, LAN, or Internet

network_cold_service_worker_benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95 over 30 unique-scope cold service-worker installations
network_cold_service_worker_benchmark.collection: Chrome DevTools Protocol with browser HTTP cache cleared and disabled; every run uses a unique page scope, service-worker script query, and Cache API name, and install fetches HTML/JavaScript/WASM from the server
network_cold_service_worker_benchmark.scope: cold service-worker installation in a unique scope with a unique cache name for each run; HTML/JavaScript/WASM are fetched from the server during install and browser HTTP cache is disabled; not service-worker update invalidation, browser HTTP-cache behavior, TLS, LAN, or Internet

network_service_worker_update_benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95 over 30 same-URL byte-different service-worker updates in unique scopes
network_service_worker_update_benchmark.collection: Chrome DevTools Protocol with browser HTTP cache cleared and disabled; each run registers worker byte version 1, requests version 2 through registration.update, waits for activation/controller takeover, and verifies both cache generations
network_service_worker_update_benchmark.scope: same-URL service-worker update from byte version 1 to byte-different version 2 in a unique scope; both generations install HTML/JavaScript/WASM, the new worker activates and controls the page, and browser HTTP cache is disabled; not browser HTTP-cache behavior, TLS, LAN, or Internet

network_http_cache_reuse_benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95 over 30 browser-HTTP-cache-reuse loads after one immutable seed load
network_http_cache_reuse_benchmark.collection: Chrome DevTools Protocol; one immutable cache-control seed load, then 30 measured loads with browser HTTP cache enabled and no service worker; static resource transfer must be zero while proof upload remains network-backed and verified
network_http_cache_reuse_benchmark.scope: normal browser HTTP-cache reuse after one immutable seed load: measured HTML/JavaScript/WASM transfers are zero, while each proof upload bypasses the cache and is cryptographically verified; not service-worker Cache Storage, TLS, LAN, or Internet

network_safari_http_cache_reuse_benchmar.scope: manual Safari normal browser HTTP-cache reuse after one immutable seed load: measured HTML/JavaScript/WASM transfers are zero, while each proof upload bypasses the cache and is cryptographically verified; not service-worker Cache Storage, TLS, LAN, or Internet

network_http_current_benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95 over 30 cache-disabled HTTP/1.1 page loads with binary proof uploads
network_http_current_benchmark.collection: Chrome DevTools Protocol with browser cache cleared and disabled; same current upload-page source as the TLS companion run
network_http_current_benchmark.scope: same-source HTTP companion to the TLS benchmark: cache-disabled code download plus cryptographically verified binary proof upload over loopback; not TLS, LAN, or Internet

network_tls_benchmark.aggregation: median, arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation, and nearest-rank P95 over 30 cache-disabled HTTPS/TLS page loads with binary proof uploads
network_tls_benchmark.collection: Chrome DevTools Protocol with browser cache cleared and disabled; the runner generates a temporary self-signed RSA-2048 127.0.0.1 certificate and Chrome ignores certificate errors
network_tls_benchmark.scope: cache-disabled TLS loopback code download plus cryptographically verified binary proof upload; not public PKI, LAN, or Internet

scope_and_limits: The primary WASM grid is a Node/V8 host measurement; the browser JSON files are automated HeadlessChrome and headed Chrome page measurements plus one manual desktop Safari 18.3 page measurement on macOS, not Android or iOS.

The CSV reports warm-start median, mean, sample standard deviation, and P95 wall time. The browser JSON files record module import and initialization after page load; the separate Chrome memory JSON records sampled renderer-JS-heap peak, not browser-process RSS or Safari/mobile peak memory.

The cache-disabled HTTP and TLS network JSONs control browser cache state over loopback. Both upload benchmarks decode and cryptographically verify the binary proof package; TLS uses a temporary self-signed certificate with Chrome certificate errors ignored. Separate service-worker benchmarks measure unique-scope cold installation, same-URL byte-update invalidation, and warmed Cache Storage hits. A separate immutable HTTP-cache benchmark measures ordinary browser-cache reuse without a service worker. No dataset measures public PKI, LAN, or Internet latency.
